{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRkquM8AAAABZTlT4Q", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5zhC6ujY", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn_T5", "number": 21, "title": "Implement DMA and HDMA A-bus I/O access restrictions", "body": "## Problem

DMA and HDMA currently access prohibited A-bus I/O addresses through ordinary, side-effecting register handlers. This can consume joypad bits, acknowledge interrupts, advance memory ports, or modify CPU/DMA registers during transfers that hardware blocks.

At baseline `03cc363011cab05992f0c2165d1c43cfef4b1764`, [`SystemBus::transfer`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/03cc363011cab05992f0c2165d1c43cfef4b1764/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L411-L418) calls unrestricted `read_raw`/`write_raw` for both endpoints. General DMA and HDMA payloads share this function. [`hdma_read`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/03cc363011cab05992f0c2165d1c43cfef4b1764/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L510-L518) also reads descriptors and indirect addresses without DMA-specific decoding.

This is a bounded prerequisite for reliable DMA/device interactions. The supplied context lists no open Issue covering it, and the recent direct-color, envelope, noise, pitch and offset improvements do not implement it.

## Expected outcome

Implement the DMA-specific A-bus access restrictions for general DMA, HDMA payloads, and HDMA descriptor/indirect-address fetches.

### Hardware semantics

The specification references are [Fullsnes](https://problemkaputt.de/fullsnes.htm), DMA transfer restrictions, and [Anomie's Register Doc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/gilligan/snesdev/master/docs/snes_registers.txt), DMA register descriptions. Both documents are already referenced by repository validation records.

In banks `$00–$3F` and `$80–$BF`, these A-bus ranges are inaccessible to DMA:

| A-bus offset | Restricted region |
| --- | --- |
| `$2100–$21FF` | B-bus register area |
| `$4000–$41FF` | Controller register area and surrounding addresses |
| `$4200–$421F` | CPU control/status registers |
| `$4300–$437F` | DMA channel registers |

Apply the following rules:

- Prohibited A-bus reads supply `$00` without invoking the underlying register read or its side effects. This is an explicit zero transfer value, not an ordinary open-bus read.
- Prohibited A-bus writes are discarded without invoking the underlying register write.
- The valid B-bus endpoint still operates: forward transfers write zero to it; reverse transfers still read it, including its normal read side effects, while discarding the prohibited A-bus write.
- Restrictions depend on the full A-bus address. Identical offsets in banks `$40–$7F` and `$C0–$FF` must retain their normal cartridge/WRAM decoding.
- Reevaluate accessibility for each byte after normal address progression. A blocked byte still consumes its transfer slot and advances the applicable count/address state. HDMA must interpret a blocked descriptor read as the returned zero terminator.
- CPU accesses retain their existing register behavior. A valid B-bus access to `$21xx` must not be rejected merely because that range is prohibited on the A-bus side.

### Focused scope and remaining work

Limit implementation to A-bus decoding and the associated suppressed side effects. Retain the existing transfer phases, device advancement, channel ordering, address wrapping and HDMA scheduling.

WRAM-to-`$2180` bus conflicts, DMA startup/alignment accuracy, HDMA initialization/overhead and first-frame behavior, same-channel contention, and exact electrical/open-bus behavior beyond the specified zero payload remain separate work. This Issue does not implement those behaviors or complete the DMA/HDMA mode-interaction matrix.

`dma` and `hdma` remain partial after this change. Retain every other supplied inventory category, scope and status; passing these checks establishes neither complete hardware accuracy nor commercial compatibility.

## Context and reproduction

A deterministic forward-transfer example uses the WRAM port as an illegal **A-bus** source:

1. Store `$5A,$12` at WRAM `$001000–$001001`; point `$2181–$2183` at `$001000`.
2. Select CGRAM address zero with `$2121`.
3. Configure channel 0 with `DMAP=$08` (forward, fixed A address, mode 0), `BBAD=$22`, `A1T=$2180`, `A1B=$00`, and count 2; start it through `$420B`.
4. Inspect CGRAM and subsequently read the WRAM port.

Expected: CGRAM entry zero receives two zero bytes, and the prohibited source reads leave the WRAM-port pointer at `$001000`. Current code instead reads `$5A,$12`, commits CGRAM `$125A`, and advances that pointer twice. This example avoids the separate conflict involving a **B-bus** `$2180` endpoint.

Existing [`machine.rs` tests](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/03cc363011cab05992f0c2165d1c43cfef4b1764/crates/snes-core/src/machine.rs#L602-L691) cover HDMA preemption, deferred NMI/device advancement, and DMA source/write boundaries, but do not exercise prohibited A-bus accesses. [`regression.rs`](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/03cc363011cab05992f0c2165d1c43cfef4b1764/crates/snes-core/tests/regression.rs#L1201-L1232) provides existing CPU-side joypad, open-bus and access-timing regressions that must remain intact.

Evaluation was limited to repository and supplied-context inspection. No implementation, builds or tests were performed during planning.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the documented exclusions for both transfer directions and all relevant DMA/HDMA A-bus read paths, including descriptor and indirect-address fetches. Record the specification sections supporting the address map, zero reads and discarded writes; distinguish specification facts from emulator timing conventions.
- [ ] Add original table-driven tests covering each prohibited range's endpoints and representative interior addresses, neighboring allowed addresses, mirrored I/O-bank boundaries, and positive cartridge/WRAM controls outside the restricted banks. Expected results must be independent of production decoding helpers.
- [ ] Verify observable side effects, not just returned bytes: prohibited reads must not shift `$4016`, acknowledge `$4210/$4211`, or advance `$2180`; prohibited writes must not alter representative CPU control and DMA channel registers. Include legal CPU-access controls.
- [ ] Test both endpoints independently: forward blocked reads still write zero to a valid B-bus port; reverse transfers still consume a valid B-bus read while suppressing the A-bus write. Include a legal B-bus port increment/readback control.
- [ ] Exercise fixed, incrementing and decrementing general-DMA addressing, transitions into/out of a prohibited range, and 16-bit A-address wrapping without bank carry. Check final address/count registers and eight-clock byte slots away from refresh boundaries.
- [ ] Exercise direct and indirect HDMA payloads, prohibited HDMA table reads, zero-descriptor termination, and table/indirect-pointer progression. Tests must show that prohibited reads cannot trigger underlying register side effects.
- [ ] Add bounded original 65C816 guest coverage through `Machine` for forward and reverse prohibited accesses, including the reproduction above. Configure and trigger transfers with executed guest instructions; assert numeric memory/register results. Generate code/data from checked-in source, require no firmware or commercial ROM, and document original MIT provenance in `tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md`.
- [ ] Record representative forward, reverse and HDMA regressions failing against the evaluation baseline and passing with the implementation. Preserve existing assertions, fixture hashes, replay durations and negative controls.
- [ ] Run the following existing Rust and source-built hardware gates successfully, using the README's documented toolchain setup:

```sh
cargo fmt --all -- --check
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings
cargo test --workspace --locked
python3 tools/make-fixture.py .cache/smoke.bin
cmp tests/roms/smoke.bin .cache/smoke.bin
python3 tools/build-test-tools.py --spc
python3 tools/hardware-tests.py \
  --ca65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ca65" \
  --ld65 "$PWD/.cache/tools/cc65/bin/ld65" \
  --spcasm "$PWD/.cache/tools/spcasm/target/release/spcasm"
python3 tools/ppu-test.py \
  --bass "$PWD/.cache/tools/bass-untech/bass/out/bass-untech"
```

- [ ] Preserve the existing browser/game regressions and pass the README browser gate. Build both audited games twice from their pinned licensed sources, retaining their hashes, then run:

```sh
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
python3 tools/build-cleared-games.py
npm --prefix web ci
npm --prefix web run build
(cd web && npx playwright install chromium)
(cd web && npm test -- --grep-invert '301 seconds')
```

  Use `SNES_TEST_PORT=18085` if necessary. Keep mandatory cleared Castle/Memory replays, Castle's complete route, Memory audio checks, freeze negative controls, diagnostic controls/SRAM checks and Pages subpath smoke enabled. Source licensing and permitted alterations remain governed by [PROVENANCE.md](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/tests/roms/PROVENANCE.md) and [CLEARED-GAMES.md](https://github.com/takahirox/snes-rust/blob/main/tests/roms/CLEARED-GAMES.md).

- [ ] Update README limitations and add a concise validation record with actual commands/results, baseline failure evidence, independent expected-value derivations and remaining DMA/HDMA gaps. Report skipped or unperformed checks honestly; mandatory acceptance must pass before merge.

## Optional validation

Additional original transfer-pattern/channel combinations beyond the required boundary and side-effect coverage. No commercial ROM acquisition is required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
